speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
क्षमा वशीकृतिर्लोके क्षमया किं न साध्यते ।
शान्तिशङ्खः करे यस्य किं करिष्यति दुर्जनः ॥
iast:
kṣamā vaśīkṛtirloke kṣamayā kiṃ na sādhyate |
śāntiśaṅkhaḥ kare yasya kiṃ kariṣyati durjanaḥ ||
english: Forgiveness wins over the world; what cannot be achieved by forgiveness? What can a wicked person do to one who holds the conch of peace in his hand?

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अतृणे पतितो वह्निः स्वयमेवोपशाम्यति ।
अक्षमावान्परं दोषैरात्मान्ं चैव योजयेत् ॥
iast:
atṛṇe patito vahniḥ svayamevopaśāmyati |
akṣamāvānparaṃ doṣairātmānṃ caiva yojayet ||
english: Fire falling where there is no grass goes out by itself; but one without forgiveness entangles others, and themselves too, in faults.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
एको धर्मः परं श्रेयः क्षमैका शान्तिरुत्तमा ।
विद्यैका परमा दृष्टिरहिंसैका सुखावहा ॥
iast:
eko dharmaḥ paraṃ śreyaḥ kṣamaikā śāntiruttamā |
vidyaikā paramā dṛṣṭirahiṃsaikā sukhāvahā ||
english: Dharma alone is the highest good; forgiveness alone is the best peace; knowledge alone is the highest vision; non-violence alone brings happiness.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ ग्रसते भूमिः सर्पो बिलशयानिव ।
राजानं चाविरोद्धारं ब्राह्मणं चाप्रवासिनम् ॥
iast:
dvāvimau grasate bhūmiḥ sarpo bilaśayāniva |
rājānaṃ cāviroddhāraṃ brāhmaṇaṃ cāpravāsinam ||
english: The earth swallows these two as a snake swallows creatures lying in their holes: a king who does not resist, and a brahmin who never leaves home.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वे कर्मणी नरः कुर्वन्नस्मिँल्लोके विरोचते ।
अब्रुवन्परुषं किं चिदसतो नार्थयंस्तथा ॥
iast:
dve karmaṇī naraḥ kurvannasmim̐lloke virocate |
abruvanparuṣaṃ kiṃ cidasato nārthayaṃstathā ||
english: A person who does two things shines in this world: speaking nothing harsh, and asking nothing of the wicked.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषव्याघ्र परप्रत्यय कारिणौ ।
स्त्रियः कामित कामिन्यो लोकः पूजित पूजकः ॥
iast:
dvāvimau puruṣavyāghra parapratyaya kāriṇau |
striyaḥ kāmita kāminyo lokaḥ pūjita pūjakaḥ ||
english: These two, tiger among men, act on the belief of others: women who desire those desired by others, and people who honour whoever is honoured.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ कण्टकौ तीक्ष्णौ शरीरपरिशोषणौ ।
यश्चाधनः कामयते यश्च कुप्यत्यनीश्वरः ॥
iast:
dvāvimau kaṇṭakau tīkṣṇau śarīrapariśoṣaṇau |
yaścādhanaḥ kāmayate yaśca kupyatyanīśvaraḥ ||
english: These two are sharp thorns that wither the body: one who is poor yet full of desires, and one who is powerless yet angry.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वावेव न विराजेते विपरीतेन कर्मणा ।
गृहस्थश्च निरारंभः कार्यवांश्चैव भिक्षुकः ॥
iast:
dvāveva na virājete viparītena karmaṇā |
gṛhasthaśca nirāraṃbhaḥ kāryavāṃścaiva bhikṣukaḥ ||
english: These two do not shine, acting against their role: a householder without enterprise, and a mendicant busy with worldly affairs.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषौ राजन्स्वर्गस्य परि तिष्ठतः ।
प्रभुश्च क्षमया युक्तो दरिद्रश्च प्रदानवान् ॥
iast:
dvāvimau puruṣau rājansvargasya pari tiṣṭhataḥ |
prabhuśca kṣamayā yukto daridraśca pradānavān ||
english: These two, king, stand above heaven: a powerful person endowed with forgiveness, and a poor person who gives.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
न्यायागतस्य द्रव्यस्य बोद्धव्यौ द्वावतिक्रमौ ।
अपात्रे प्रतिपत्तिश्च पात्रे चाप्रतिपादनम् ॥
iast:
nyāyāgatasya dravyasya boddhavyau dvāvatikramau |
apātre pratipattiśca pātre cāpratipādanam ||
english: Of wealth honestly gained, two misuses should be understood: giving it to the unworthy, and not giving it to the worthy.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वावंभसि निवेष्टव्यौ गले बद्ध्वा दृढं शिलाम् ।
धनवन्तमदातारं दरिद्रं चातपस्विनम् ॥
iast:
dvāvaṃbhasi niveṣṭavyau gale baddhvā dṛḍhaṃ śilām |
dhanavantamadātāraṃ daridraṃ cātapasvinam ||
english: These two should be thrown into the water with a stone tied firmly to the neck: a rich person who does not give, and a poor person who does not practise austerity.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
द्वाविमौ पुरुषव्याघ्र सुर्यमण्डलभेदिनौ ।
परिव्राड्योगयुक्तश्च रणे चाभिमुखो हतः ॥
iast:
dvāvimau puruṣavyāghra suryamaṇḍalabhedinau |
parivrāḍyogayuktaśca raṇe cābhimukho hataḥ ||
english: These two, tiger among men, pierce the disc of the sun: a wandering ascetic joined in yoga, and one slain in battle while facing the enemy.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
त्रयो न्याया मनुष्याणां श्रूयन्ते भरतर्षभ ।
कनीयान्मध्यमः श्रेष्ठ इति वेदविदो विदुः ॥
iast:
trayo nyāyā manuṣyāṇāṃ śrūyante bharatarṣabha |
kanīyānmadhyamaḥ śreṣṭha iti vedavido viduḥ ||
english: Three courses of conduct are spoken of among people, best of the Bharatas: the lesser, the middling and the best. So the knowers of the Veda say.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
त्रिविधाः पुरुषा राजन्नुत्तमाधममध्यमाः ।
नियोजयेद्यथावत्तांस्त्रिविधेष्वेव कर्मसु ॥
iast:
trividhāḥ puruṣā rājannuttamādhamamadhyamāḥ |
niyojayedyathāvattāṃstrividheṣveva karmasu ||
english: People are of three kinds, king: the best, the lowest and the middling. One should assign them properly to the three kinds of work.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
त्रय एवाधना राजन्भार्या दासस्तथा सुतः ।
यत्ते समधिगच्छन्ति यस्य ते तस्य तद्धनम् ॥
iast:
traya evādhanā rājanbhāryā dāsastathā sutaḥ |
yatte samadhigacchanti yasya te tasya taddhanam ||
english: Three own no wealth, king: a wife, a slave and a son. Whatever they earn belongs to the one they belong to.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
हरणं च परस्वानां परदाराभिमर्शनम् ।
सुहृदश्च परित्यागस्त्रयो दोषा क्षयावहः ॥
iast:
haraṇaṃ ca parasvānāṃ paradārābhimarśanam |
suhṛdaśca parityāgastrayo doṣā kṣayāvahaḥ ||
english: Taking what belongs to others, assaulting another's wife and abandoning a friend: these three faults bring ruin.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
त्रिविधं नरकस्येदं द्वारं नाशनमात्मनः ।
कामः क्रोधस्तथा लोभस्तस्मादेतत्त्रयं त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
trividhaṃ narakasyedaṃ dvāraṃ nāśanamātmanaḥ |
kāmaḥ krodhastathā lobhastasmādetattrayaṃ tyajet ||
english: This threefold gate of hell destroys the self: desire, anger and greed. So one should give up these three.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
वरप्रदानं राज्यां च पुत्रजन्म च भारत ।
शत्रोश्च मोक्षणं कृच्छ्रात्त्रीणि चैकं च तत्समम् ॥
iast:
varapradānaṃ rājyāṃ ca putrajanma ca bhārata |
śatrośca mokṣaṇaṃ kṛcchrāttrīṇi caikaṃ ca tatsamam ||
english: Receiving a boon, gaining a kingdom and the birth of a son, Bharata: these three, and a fourth, rescuing an enemy from distress, are equal.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
भक्तं च बजमानं च तवास्मीति वादिनम् ।
त्रीनेतान् शरणं प्राप्तान्विषमेऽपि न सन्त्यजेत् ॥
iast:
bhaktaṃ ca bajamānaṃ ca tavāsmīti vādinam |
trīnetān śaraṇaṃ prāptānviṣame'pi na santyajet ||
english: The devoted, the one who serves you, and the one who says 'I am yours': these three, having come for refuge, should not be abandoned even in hard times.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चत्वारि राज्ञा तु महाबलेन
वर्ज्यान्याहुः पण्डितस्तानि विद्यात् ।
अल्पप्रज्ञैः सह मन्त्रं न कुर्यान्
न दीर्घसूत्रैरलसैश्चारणैश्च ॥
iast:
catvāri rājñā tu mahābalena
varjyānyāhuḥ paṇḍitastāni vidyāt |
alpaprajñaiḥ saha mantraṃ na kuryān
na dīrghasūtrairalasaiścāraṇaiśca ||
english: The wise say a mighty king should avoid four; let him know them: he should not take counsel with those of little understanding, with procrastinators, with the lazy, or with flatterers.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चत्वारि ते तात गृहे वसन्तु
श्रियाभिजुष्टस्य गृहस्थ धर्मे ।
वृद्धो ज्ञातिरवसन्नः कुलीनः
सखा दरिद्रो भगिनी चानपत्या ॥
iast:
catvāri te tāta gṛhe vasantu
śriyābhijuṣṭasya gṛhastha dharme |
vṛddho jñātiravasannaḥ kulīnaḥ
sakhā daridro bhaginī cānapatyā ||
english: Dear one, let four live in your house, you who are blessed with fortune and follow the householder's dharma: an aged relative, a person of good family fallen on hard times, a poor friend, and a sister without children.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चत्वार्याह महाराज सद्यस्कानि बृहस्पतिः ।
पृच्छते त्रिदशेन्द्राय तानीमानि निबोध मे ॥
iast:
catvāryāha mahārāja sadyaskāni bṛhaspatiḥ |
pṛcchate tridaśendrāya tānīmāni nibodha me ||
english: Brihaspati, great king, spoke of four things that bear fruit at once, when asked by the lord of the gods. Learn them from me:

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
देवतानां च सङ्कल्पमनुभावं च धीमताम् ।
विनयं कृतविद्यानां विनाशं पापकर्मणाम् ॥
iast:
devatānāṃ ca saṅkalpamanubhāvaṃ ca dhīmatām |
vinayaṃ kṛtavidyānāṃ vināśaṃ pāpakarmaṇām ||
english: the resolve of the gods, the power of the wise, the humility of the learned, and the ruin of those who do evil.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
चत्वारि कर्माण्यभयङ्कराणि
भयं प्रयच्छन्त्ययथाकृतानि ।
मानाग्निहोत्रं उत मानमौनं
मानेनाधीतमुत मानयज्ञः ॥
iast:
catvāri karmāṇyabhayaṅkarāṇi
bhayaṃ prayacchantyayathākṛtāni |
mānāgnihotraṃ uta mānamaunaṃ
mānenādhītamuta mānayajñaḥ ||
english: Four acts that remove fear bring fear when not done properly: the fire offering done for pride, silence kept for pride, study done for pride, and sacrifice done for pride.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पञ्चाग्नयो मनुष्येण परिचर्याः प्रयत्नतः ।
पिता माताग्निरात्मा च गुरुश्च भरतर्षभ ॥
iast:
pañcāgnayo manuṣyeṇa paricaryāḥ prayatnataḥ |
pitā mātāgnirātmā ca guruśca bharatarṣabha ||
english: Five fires should be tended by a person with care: father, mother, the sacred fire, oneself and the teacher, best of the Bharatas.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पञ्चैव पूजयँल्लोके यशः प्राप्नोति केवलम् ।
देवान्पितॄन्मनुष्यांश्च भिक्षूनतिथिपञ्चमान् ॥
iast:
pañcaiva pūjayam̐lloke yaśaḥ prāpnoti kevalam |
devānpitṝnmanuṣyāṃśca bhikṣūnatithipañcamān ||
english: Honouring five alone, one gains fame in the world: the gods, the ancestors, people, mendicants, and guests as the fifth.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पञ्च त्वानुगमिष्यन्ति यत्र यत्र गमिष्यसि ।
मित्राण्यमित्रा मध्यस्था उपजीव्योपजीविनः ॥
iast:
pañca tvānugamiṣyanti yatra yatra gamiṣyasi |
mitrāṇyamitrā madhyasthā upajīvyopajīvinaḥ ||
english: Five will follow you wherever you go: friends, enemies, the neutral, those who live on you and those you live on.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
पञ्चेन्द्रियस्य मर्त्यस्य छिद्रं चेदेकमिन्द्रियम् ।
ततोऽस्य स्रवति प्रज्ञा दृतेः पादादिवोदकम् ॥
iast:
pañcendriyasya martyasya chidraṃ cedekamindriyam |
tato'sya sravati prajñā dṛteḥ pādādivodakam ||
english: If one of a mortal's five senses has a hole, through it their wisdom flows out, like water from the foot of a leather bag.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षड्दोषाः पुरुषेणेह हातव्या भूतिमिच्छता ।
निद्रा तन्द्री भयं क्रोध आलस्यं दीर्घसूत्रता ॥
iast:
ṣaḍdoṣāḥ puruṣeṇeha hātavyā bhūtimicchatā |
nidrā tandrī bhayaṃ krodha ālasyaṃ dīrghasūtratā ||
english: Six faults should be given up here by a person who wants to prosper: too much sleep, drowsiness, fear, anger, laziness and procrastination.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षडिमान्पुरुषो जह्याद्भिन्नां नावमिवार्णवे ।
अप्रवक्तारमाचार्यमनधीयानमृत्विजम् ॥
iast:
ṣaḍimānpuruṣo jahyādbhinnāṃ nāvamivārṇave |
apravaktāramācāryamanadhīyānamṛtvijam ||
english: A person should give up these six, like a leaking boat at sea: a teacher who does not teach, a priest who has not studied,

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अरक्षितारं राजानं भार्यां चाप्रिय वादिनीम् ।
ग्रामकारं च गोपालं वनकामं च नापितम् ॥
iast:
arakṣitāraṃ rājānaṃ bhāryāṃ cāpriya vādinīm |
grāmakāraṃ ca gopālaṃ vanakāmaṃ ca nāpitam ||
english: a king who does not protect, a wife who speaks unkindly, a cowherd who wants to live in the village, and a barber who wants to live in the forest.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षडेव तु गुणाः पुंसा न हातव्याः कदाचन ।
सत्यं दानमनालस्यमनसूया क्षमा धृतिः ॥
iast:
ṣaḍeva tu guṇāḥ puṃsā na hātavyāḥ kadācana |
satyaṃ dānamanālasyamanasūyā kṣamā dhṛtiḥ ||
english: Six qualities a person should never give up: truthfulness, generosity, diligence, freedom from envy, forbearance and steadiness.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
अर्थागमो नित्यमरोगिता च
प्रिया च भार्या प्रियवादिनी च ।
वश्यश्च पुत्रोऽर्थकरी च विद्या
षट् जीवलोकस्य सुखानि राजन् ॥
iast:
arthāgamo nityamarogitā ca
priyā ca bhāryā priyavādinī ca |
vaśyaśca putro'rthakarī ca vidyā
ṣaṭ jīvalokasya sukhāni rājan ||
english: A steady income, constant good health, a beloved and sweet-spoken wife, an obedient son and knowledge that earns a living: these, king, are the six joys of the world of the living.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षण्णामात्मनि नित्यानामैश्वर्यं योऽधिगच्छति ।
न स पापैः कुतोऽनर्थैर्युज्यते विजितेन्द्रियः ॥
iast:
ṣaṇṇāmātmani nityānāmaiśvaryaṃ yo'dhigacchati |
na sa pāpaiḥ kuto'narthairyujyate vijitendriyaḥ ||
english: One who gains mastery over the six that always dwell within, having conquered the senses, is not touched by sins, let alone by misfortunes.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षडिमे षट्सु जीवन्ति सप्तमो नोपलभ्यते ।
चोराः प्रमत्ते जीवन्ति व्याधितेषु चिकित्सकाः ॥
iast:
ṣaḍime ṣaṭsu jīvanti saptamo nopalabhyate |
corāḥ pramatte jīvanti vyādhiteṣu cikitsakāḥ ||
english: These six live off six; a seventh is not found: thieves live off the careless, doctors off the sick,

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
प्रमदाः कामयानेषु यजमानेषु याजकाः ।
राजा विवदमानेषु नित्यं मूर्खेषु पण्डिताः ॥
iast:
pramadāḥ kāmayāneṣu yajamāneṣu yājakāḥ |
rājā vivadamāneṣu nityaṃ mūrkheṣu paṇḍitāḥ ||
english: women off the lustful, priests off those who sacrifice, the king off those who quarrel, and the learned always off fools.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षडिमानि विनश्यन्ति मुहूर्तमनवेक्षणात् ।
गावः सेवा कृषिर्भार्या विद्या वृषलसंगतिः ॥
iast:
ṣaḍimāni vinaśyanti muhūrtamanavekṣaṇāt |
gāvaḥ sevā kṛṣirbhāryā vidyā vṛṣalasaṃgatiḥ ||
english: These six are ruined by a moment's neglect: cows, service, farming, a wife, learning and company with a shudra.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
षडेते ह्यवमन्यन्ते नित्यं पूर्वोपकारिणम् ।
आचार्यं शिक्षिता शिष्याः कृतदारश्च मातरम् ॥
iast:
ṣaḍete hyavamanyante nityaṃ pūrvopakāriṇam |
ācāryaṃ śikṣitā śiṣyāḥ kṛtadāraśca mātaram ||
english: These six always disregard one who once helped them: students, once taught, their teacher; a married man his mother;

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
नारिं विगतकामस्तु कृतार्थाश्च प्रयोजकम् ।
नावं निस्तीर्णकान्तारा नातुराश्च चिकित्सकम् ॥
iast:
nāriṃ vigatakāmastu kṛtārthāśca prayojakam |
nāvaṃ nistīrṇakāntārā nāturāśca cikitsakam ||
english: a man whose desire is spent, the woman; those whose aim is achieved, the one who helped; those who have crossed the wilderness, the boat; and the cured, their doctor.

speaker: Vidura
devanagari:
आरोग्यमानृण्यमविप्रवासः
सद्भिर्मनुष्यैः सह संप्रयोगः ।
स्वप्रत्यया वृत्तिरभीतवासः
षट् जीवलोकस्य सुखानि राजन् ॥
iast:
ārogyamānṛṇyamavipravāsaḥ
sadbhirmanuṣyaiḥ saha saṃprayogaḥ |
svapratyayā vṛttirabhītavāsaḥ
ṣaṭ jīvalokasya sukhāni rājan ||
english: Health, freedom from debt, not living abroad, the company of good people, a livelihood of one's own, and living without fear: these, king, are the six joys of the world of the living.
